docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The Redu homepage introduces the platform to refugee learners, families, and NGO partners in Uganda. It explains the core product features and separates public information from the student learning application.

Live link: Redu Informational Website

docs.title: Main Message
docs.text:
Learning that keeps going.

Redu delivers curriculum-grounded lessons, simple explanations, and offline support for low-connectivity environments.

docs.title: 1. Hero & onboarding
docs.text: Introduces the value proposition ("Learning should not stop at the edge of a weak signal") and provides direct onboarding links for students.

docs.title: 2. Core pillars
docs.text:
• Curriculum-grounded: Aligned with the Ugandan secondary-school curriculum (English and Sciences).
  • Personal tutor: Simplified, language-aware explanations for multilingual learners.
  • Offline-first: Lightweight downloads built for shared devices and expensive mobile data.
  • Formative assessments: Feedback focused on understanding mistakes rather than just scores.

docs.title: 3. Team & contact
docs.text: Introduces the Techsus development team and provides a contact form to capture NGO and educational partnerships.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Redu is a Progressive Web App (PWA) backed by a single, centralized Redu API. There is one PWA for everyone: learners and administrators sign in through the same interface, and role-based access control (RBAC) decides which screens and features each user sees. Redu is web-only; there is no native mobile app.

The Learn and Assessments modules use a shared AI Service, which finds the right curriculum Markdown file, passes its file URI to Gemini 3.8 Flash, and returns content generated from the available files. Only the Redu API reads from or writes to the database.

  • Client Application: One PWA (learner and admin share the same sign-in and interface), deployed on Vercel. [Add: frontend framework, e.g. React / Next.js]
  • Backend Integration Layer: FastAPI, deployed on Heroku.
  • Persistence Layer: PostgreSQL database on Heroku.
  • AI Integration & Grounding: Google Gemini 3.8 Flash, grounded on curriculum Markdown files stored in the Gemini Files API.
  • Offline Storage: IndexedDB in the learner's browser, which holds downloaded lessons for offline use.

The PWA talks only to the Redu API. Modules never call each other, the AI Service never calls back into a module, and no module reads or writes the database directly.

docs.title: System Architecture Diagram
docs.text: System Architecture diagram (Lucidspark): Redu System Architecture Diagram

docs.title: Progressive Web App (PWA)
docs.text:
The single client application, deployed on Vercel. It can be installed on a phone or computer and works offline for downloaded lessons. After sign-in, the PWA shows learner screens or administrator screens depending on the user's role.

  • Learner view: select a subject, topic and lesson; read AI-generated lesson content; take diagnostics, practice sets and quizzes; view progress; download lessons for offline use.
  • Admin view: system management, usage and engagement analytics.

docs.title: Redu API (FastAPI)
docs.text: The central engine of the system, deployed on Heroku. It signs users in, checks their role, routes each request to the right module, validates data and is the only component that talks to PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Feature Modules
docs.text: Module What it does Uses the AI Service Learn Lists subjects, topics and lessons, generates lesson content, answers learner questions and records lesson progress. Yes Assessments Starts assessments, evaluates answers, gives feedback and a catch-up plan. Yes View Progress Shows completed lessons and evaluation results. No Offline Packages Prepares downloadable lessons and returns them to the learner's device. No System Management Provides system-wide usage and engagement data to the administrator. No

docs.title: AI Service
docs.text: Shared by the Learn and Assessments modules. It looks through the curriculum Markdown files, extracts the file URI of the right file, sends the URI and a prompt to Gemini 3.8 Flash, and returns the generated content to the module that asked. It never touches the database and never calls a module.

docs.title: Curriculum Markdown Files and Gemini Files API
docs.text: Lesson text is stored as Markdown files (with the related textbook images in PNG/JPEG) in a folder in the backend. A one-time seed/import script uploads them to the Gemini Files API, which manages and retrieves them for the AI.

docs.title: Database (PostgreSQL)
docs.text: Stores learner data, topics, learning content, assessments, progress, tutor interactions, offline packages and sync events. It is accessed only by the Redu API.

docs.title: Offline Storage (IndexedDB)
docs.text: A browser database on the learner's device. Lessons the learner downloads while online are copied here so they can be opened later without internet.

docs.title: Learning Flow (core flow)
docs.text:
[ Learner selects subject, topic, lesson ]
                   │
                   ▼
 [ PWA ] ──► [ Redu API ] ──► [ Learn module ] ──► [ AI Service ]
                                                      │
                                   finds the Markdown file and extracts its file URI
                                                      │
                                                      ▼
                                       [ Gemini 3.8 Flash ]
                           (file URI + prompt → content generated from the available files)
                                                      │
                                                      ▼
 [ Learner sees the lesson ] ◄── [ PWA ] ◄── [ Redu API ] ◄── [ Learn module ]
                                                  │
                                                  ▼
                                   [ Database: progress and content saved ]
1. Choose: The learner selects a subject, a topic and a lesson in the PWA. 2. Request: The PWA sends the request to the Redu API, which passes it to the Learn module. 3. Find the file: The Learn module calls the AI Service. The AI Service goes through the curriculum Markdown files and extracts the file URI for the chosen lesson. 4. Generate: The AI Service sends the file URI and a prompt to Gemini 3.8 Flash. Gemini generates the content using only the available curriculum files and returns it. 5. Show and save: The content goes back through the Redu API to the PWA. The Redu API saves the lesson content and the learner's progress in PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Assessment Flow
docs.text:
1. The learner starts an assessment. The Assessments module asks the AI Service for questions based on the lesson's Markdown file.
  2. The learner submits answers. The AI Service evaluates them against the same content and returns the result, feedback, correct answers and a catch-up plan.
  3. The Redu API saves the evaluation results and progress, and they appear in View Progress.

docs.title: Curriculum Loading Flow (one-time seed script)
docs.text:
1. The team runs a seed/import script once, using the curriculum folders kept in the backend (Markdown lesson files and textbook images).
  2. The script uploads the files to the Gemini Files API.
  3. The script saves topics and lessons through the Redu API into the database.
  4. The same script is run again only when the Markdown files change. Admins do not upload content through the interface.

docs.title: Offline Flow
docs.text:
[ Learner online ] ──► [ Offline Packages module via Redu API ] ──► [ PWA ]
                                                                       │
                                                      copies lessons into [ IndexedDB ]
                                                                       │
 [ Learner offline ] ◄────── opens saved lessons from IndexedDB ◄─────┘
1. While online, the learner chooses lessons to download. 2. The Offline Packages module returns the downloaded lessons through the Redu API. 3. The PWA copies the lessons into IndexedDB on the device. 4. While offline, the learner opens the saved lessons from IndexedDB without any network request. 5. Once the device is online again, offline activity is sent to the Redu API and saved.

docs.title: Administrator Flow
docs.text: The administrator signs in on the same PWA. The System Management module requests usage and engagement data from the Redu API, which reads it from PostgreSQL and returns system analytics.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Redu backend is a FastAPI service that stores learner accounts, the curriculum, assessments and progress, and connects the Redu PWA to the AI tutor. It runs on Heroku and keeps its data in PostgreSQL.

Repository: techsus-backend

Live API: https://herokuapp.com

API documentation: https://herokuapp.com/docs

The backend has three main jobs:

  • Serve the curriculum (subjects, topics, lessons and questions) for the learner's class level
  • Mark assessments and track progress using Redu rules, never the AI
  • Answer learner questions through the AI tutor, grounded only on curriculum records

docs.title: Tech stack
docs.text: Part Technology Framework FastAPI (Python) Database PostgreSQL AI service Google Gemini API and Gemini Files API Hosting Heroku Package manager uv Code quality Ruff and pytest (see Code Standards)

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Python, uv, Git, a PostgreSQL database and a Gemini API key.

git clone https://github.com.git
cd techsus-backend
uv sync

Create a .env file in the repository root with the variables from section 4.5, then start the server:

uv run fastapi dev

The API runs at http://127.0.0.1:8000 and the interactive documentation is at http://127.0.0.

docs.title: Database schema
docs.text:
The data model has eight tables. User ids are UUIDs created on the device or the server, so the same account works across devices and offline.

Table What it stores users Every person on the platform: students and administrators. Holds display name, role, class level, hashed password and optional email topics The curriculum outline. One row per topic, with its subject, class level, term, title and order learning_content Lessons, examples and the question bank, tagged to a topic. The AI tutor is grounded only on this table learner_assessments One row per diagnostic, practice set or quiz attempt, with answers, score, gaps found and the catch-up plan learner_progress How far each student has got in each topic, mastery percentage and which lessons are completed ai_tutor_interactions Each question a student asks the AI tutor and the answer, with an option to save it for offline reading offline_packages Downloadable bundles of lessons, exercises and tests for use without internet sync_events A log of every time a device syncs offline progress or downloads a package

docs.title: Main relationships
docs.text: From To Relationship topics learning_content One topic has many lessons and questions users learner_assessments One student has many attempts over time users and topics learner_progress One student has one progress record per topic users ai_tutor_interactions One student has many tutor interactions learning_content ai_tutor_interactions Each answer is grounded on one curriculum record users sync_events One student's device can sync many times offline_packages sync_events One package can be downloaded by many learners

docs.title: 4.5 Environment variables
docs.text:
Secrets are never committed to the repository. Locally they are kept in a .env file that is listed in .gitignore. On Heroku they are set under Settings, then Config Vars.

Variable Description DATABASE_URL Connection string for the PostgreSQL database REDU_AUTH_SECRET Secret key used to sign login tokens GEMINI_API_KEY Key for the Gemini AI tutor service

See Deployment & DevOps for the frontend variable and the production setup.

docs.title: Live API docs
docs.text:
FastAPI generates interactive documentation from the code. Every endpoint can be tried directly from the page by selecting Try it out.

Environment Address Local http://127.0.0 Production https://herokuapp.com/docs

The page also lists the request and response schemas at the bottom, for example AITutorConversationSummary.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Endpoints are grouped under /api/v1. The topics endpoints and the health check are shown below. The remaining groups (users, assessments, progress, AI tutor, offline packages and sync) are listed with their parameters on the /docs page, which always matches the running code.

Method Path Purpose GET /health Confirms the service is running GET /api/v1/topics List topics GET /api/v1/topics/{topic_id} Get one topic PATCH /api/v1/topics/{topic_id} Update a topic DELETE /api/v1/topics/{topic_id} Deactivate a topic

docs.title: Example API usage
docs.text:
Request: 

GET /api/v1/topics/3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6

Response, 200 OK: 

{
  "topic_id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
  "subject_name": "Mathematics",
  "class_level": "S1",
  "term": 1,
  "title": "Quadratic Equations",
  "sequence_no": 3,
  "created_at": "2026-08-28T11:37:48.770Z"
}

Health check: 

GET https://herokuapp.com/health

A healthy service returns 200 OK.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
When a request breaks a schema rule, FastAPI returns 422 Unprocessable Entity with the exact field and reason. Example: updating a topic with a class level that does not exist.

{
  "detail": [
    {
      "type": "enum",
      "loc": ["body", "class_level"],
      "msg": "Input should be 'S1' or 'S2'",
      "input": "S5",
      "ctx": { "expected": "'S1' or 'S2'" }
    }
  ]
}
Status Meaning 200 OK The request succeeded 404 Not Found The record does not exist 422 Unprocessable Entity The request data is missing or invalid

docs.title: Security and authentication
docs.text: Area How it is handled Passwords Stored only as a hash. The real password is never saved Roles Each user is a student or an admin, and the role decides what they can access Login tokens Signed with REDU_AUTH_SECRET Secrets Kept in environment variables, never in the code AI key GEMINI_API_KEY stays on the server and is never sent to the browser AI answers The tutor is grounded only on learning_content, to prevent off-syllabus answers Scoring Answers are marked by Redu rules, never by the AI Transport All traffic uses HTTPS

docs.title: Testing and code quality
docs.text:
The backend is checked on every pull request with lint, format and test commands:

uv run --no-sync ruff check .
uv run --no-sync ruff format --check .
uv run --no-sync pytest --cov --cov-report=term-missing

Tests cover happy path, negative, boundary and edge cases. The full rules are in Code Standards.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: The backend is deployed on Heroku when a change is merged into main. Steps, rollback and troubleshooting are in Deployment & DevOps.

docs.title: 2.1 Purpose
docs.text:
Redu’s brand guidelines ensure that the informational website and student PWA look and feel like one consistent product. The design should communicate trust, continuity and possibility while remaining clear and accessible for refugee secondary-school learners in Uganda.

Redu should feel:

  • Supportive.
  • Professional.
  • Hopeful.
  • Simple.
  • Respectful, not pity-driven.

The central brand message is:

Learning that keeps going.

docs.title: 2.2 Brand Positioning
docs.text:
Redu is an offline-first, curriculum-grounded learning platform for refugee secondary-school learners in Uganda. It provides structured lessons, practice, simpler explanations, progress support and AI-assisted tutoring when internet access or learning resources are limited.

Redu supports schools and learners; it does not replace teachers or national education systems.

docs.title: 2.3 Logo Inspiration and Development
docs.text:
The Redu logo is inspired by the image of an open door. The door represents access, opportunity and a pathway towards a better future through education.

For refugee secondary-school learners, education can be interrupted by displacement, language barriers, limited resources and unreliable connectivity. The open door symbol communicates that these challenges should not permanently close a learner’s educational journey. Redu is designed to help learners find a way forward and continue learning.

The logo represents:

  • Access: making learning materials easier to reach.
  • Opportunity: opening pathways to further education and future careers.
  • Progress: helping learners move forward one lesson and topic at a time.
  • Welcome: creating a learning space where learners feel supported.
  • Continuity: keeping education open even when learning is interrupted.

The door also connects with Redu’s purpose as a bridge between the learner and educational support. Through curriculum-grounded lessons, practice, simpler explanations and offline access, Redu helps learners move through barriers that may otherwise limit their progress.

The logo was designed to be simple and recognisable across the informational website, student PWA, browser icon, offline packages, printed material and presentation documents. The blue communicates trust and stability, while the maroon accent adds warmth, confidence and distinction.

The final logo concept can be described as:

An open door to continued learning and future opportunity.

docs.title: 2.4 Colour Palette
docs.text:
Redu uses deep blue, cool white and maroon to create a mature, calm and trustworthy visual identity.

Colour Hex value Use Redu Blue #17365D Headings, navigation and primary buttons Deep Blue #0F2747 Dark sections and hover states Cool White #F7F9FC Main background Pure White #FFFFFF Cards and content surfaces Border Grey #D8E0EA Borders and dividers

docs.title: 2.5 Typography
docs.text:
Typography must remain readable on small smartphones, tablets and desktop screens. Use one primary sans-serif font across the website and PWA.

Text level Use Display heading Hero messages and major statements Page heading Main page and learning-area titles Section heading Separating content sections Body text Explanations and lesson content Label Forms and controls Helper text Additional guidance Status text Progress, offline and error messages

Use clear headings, comfortable line spacing and sufficient space between lesson sections.

docs.title: 2.6 Buttons and Components
docs.text:
Buttons should describe the action clearly:

For the informational website

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This section describes the rules every contributor follows so the Redu codebase stays consistent, readable and safe to change. In both the backend and the frontend, these rules are not only guidelines. They are checked automatically, and code that fails the checks cannot be merged.

Frontend repository: techsus-frontend

Backend repository: techsus-backend

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: Part Tool Purpose Backend Ruff (ruff check) Linting: finds bugs, unused code and bad patterns Backend Ruff (ruff format) Formatting: keeps the code style identical across the team Backend pytest and pytest-cov Runs the automated tests and measures coverage Backend uv Runs every tool inside the project environment Frontend npm lint script Linting: finds errors and bad patterns in the Next.js code Frontend Prettier 3.6.2 Formatting: keeps the code style identical across the team Frontend npm build script Confirms the whole app compiles for production

docs.title: Backend checks
docs.text:
Run these three commands from the root of the backend repository before every push. They are the same commands the CI/CD pipeline runs.

uv run --no-sync ruff check .
uv run --no-sync ruff format --check .
uv run --no-sync pytest --cov --cov-report=term-missing
Command What it does ruff check . Lints every file and lists problems ruff format --check . Reports files that are not formatted correctly, without changing them pytest --cov --cov-report=term-missing Runs all tests and prints which lines are not covered by a test

The --no-sync flag tells uv to use the environment as it is, without reinstalling packages first. This keeps the run fast and makes it behave the same way in CI.

If a check fails, these commands fix most issues automatically:

uv run ruff check . --fix
uv run ruff format .

Then run the three checks again to confirm everything passes.

docs.title: Frontend checks
docs.text:
Run these commands from the root of the frontend repository before every push.

npm install
npm run lint
npx prettier@3.6.2 --check .
npm run build
Command What it does npm install Installs the exact packages the project needs npm run lint Checks the code for errors and bad patterns npx prettier@3.6.2 --check . Reports files that are not formatted correctly, without changing them npm run build Compiles the app for production and fails if anything is broken

The Prettier version is fixed at 3.6.2, so every developer and the CI/CD pipeline format the code in exactly the same way.

If the format check fails, this command fixes the formatting automatically:

npx prettier@3.6.2 --write .

Then run the checks again to confirm everything passes.

A passing build matters for a PWA, because a broken build would stop learners from receiving updates.

docs.title: CI/CD enforcement
docs.text:
The same checks run automatically on every pull request, in both repositories.

  1. A developer opens a pull request.
  2. The pipeline runs the checks for that repository: lint, format check and tests for the backend, lint, format check and build for the frontend.
  3. If any step fails, the pull request is marked as failed and must be fixed before merging.
  4. When all steps pass and a teammate approves, the change can be merged into main.
  5. The merge triggers deployment, as described in Deployment & DevOps.
Backend:   push --> lint --> format check --> tests + coverage --> review --> merge --> deploy
Frontend:  push --> lint --> format check --> build --> review --> merge --> deploy

Because the checks run on every pull request, broken or badly formatted code never reaches production.

docs.title: Backend (Python)
docs.text: Area Rule Files and functions snake_case, for example get_topic Classes and schemas PascalCase, for example AITutorConversationSummary Constants UPPER_SNAKE_CASE Type hints Add type hints to function parameters and return values Routes Group under /api/v1 and give each route a clear summary for the /docs page

docs.title: Frontend (Next.js)
docs.text: Area Rule Components PascalCase names and files, for example LessonCard Functions and variables camelCase, for example getLessons Constants UPPER_SNAKE_CASE Components Keep them small and focused on one job Environment variables Use NEXT_PUBLIC_ only for values that are safe to show in the browser

docs.title: Both
docs.text: Area Rule Names Use clear names. Write topic_id or topicId, not t Functions Do one job and stay short enough to read without scrolling Comments Explain why something is done, not what the code already says Secrets Never write keys, passwords or tokens in code. Read them from environment variables Unused code Delete it instead of commenting it out

docs.title: Testing standards
docs.text:
Every new feature or bug fix comes with tests. A good test set covers four kinds of cases:

Type What it checks Example Happy path The normal, correct use Get a topic that exists and receive 200 Negative Wrong or invalid input Get a topic that does not exist and receive 404 Boundary Limits of allowed values Smallest and largest accepted values Edge Unusual but possible situations Empty list of topics, missing optional fields

Backend test files are named test_*.py, and each test name describes the situation it covers. The coverage report from --cov-report=term-missing lists lines with no test, and contributors use it to find gaps.

docs.title: Git and review standards
docs.text: Rule Detail Branches Work on a separate branch, never directly on main Commits Small commits with a short message that says what changed Pull requests One purpose per pull request, with a clear description Review At least one teammate reviews before merging Checks All CI checks must pass before merging

docs.title: Pre-merge checklist
docs.text:
Before asking for a review, confirm that:

  • Backend: ruff check . and ruff format --check . pass
  • Backend: all tests pass and new code has tests
  • Frontend: npm run lint, npx prettier@3.6.2 --check . and npm run build pass
  • No secrets or .env files are committed
  • The pull request description explains the change

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This section explains how the Redu platform is built, deployed and monitored. It covers the Next.js PWA frontend, the FastAPI backend on Heroku and the database, and it is written so a new team member can ship a change without help.

Frontend repository: techsus-frontend

Backend repository: techsus-backend

Backend API: https://redu-8a6d68a6558b.herokuapp.com

API documentation: https://redu-8a6d68a6558b.herokuapp.com/docs

docs.title: Deployment architecture
docs.text:
Learner device (phone, tablet, school computer)
        |
        |  HTTPS
        v
[Vercel]  ---> Redu PWA (Next.js, service worker for offline use)
        |
        |  HTTPS / REST (/api/v1/...)
        v
[Heroku]  ---> FastAPI backend
        |
        +----------------------+
        |                      |
        v                      v
[PostgreSQL database]    [Google Gemini API]
Learners, topics,        Curriculum-based
progress, conversations  AI tutor

Note

The AI tutor works online only. Lessons, quizzes and progress work offline and sync when the connection returns.

docs.title: Environments
docs.text: Environment Frontend Backend Local http://localhost:3000 http://127.0.0.1:8000 Production Vercel heroku

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Secrets are never committed to the repository. They are set in the hosting dashboard for each service, and locally in a .env file that is listed in .gitignore.

docs.title: Backend (Heroku)
docs.text: Variable Description DATABASE_URL Connection string for the PostgreSQL database REDU_AUTH_SECRET Secret key used to sign login tokens GEMINI_API_KEY Key for the Gemini AI tutor service

docs.title: Frontend (Vercel)
docs.text:
Variable Description NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL Address of the backend API

Warning

Variables that start with NEXT_PUBLIC_ are included in the browser code and can be seen by anyone. Never put a secret in one.

docs.title: Frontend deployment
docs.text:
The Next.js frontend is deployed on Vercel and served over HTTPS. HTTPS is required for a PWA, because browsers only allow service workers on secure connections.

Build locally to check that everything compiles:

npm install
npm run build

Deployment steps:

  1. Connect the techsus-frontend repository to Vercel.
  2. Add NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL with the backend address from section 8.1.
  3. Merge into main. Vercel builds and publishes the new version automatically.

docs.title: PWA update behaviour
docs.text: When a new version is published, the service worker downloads it in the background. Learners get the new version the next time they reopen the app. Downloaded lesson packages stay on the device during an update.

docs.title: Backend deployment
docs.text:
The FastAPI backend runs on Heroku. A Procfile at the root of the backend repository tells Heroku how to start the app.

Deployment steps:

  1. Connect the techsus-backend repository to the Heroku app.
  2. Add DATABASE_URL, REDU_AUTH_SECRET and GEMINI_API_KEY under Settings, then Config Vars.
  3. Merge into main to trigger a deployment.
  4. Call the health endpoint to confirm the service is running.

docs.title: Health check
docs.text:
GET https://redu-8a6d68a6558b.herokuapp.com/health

A healthy service returns 200 OK with a JSON response. The same endpoint can be tried from the API documentation page under the default section by selecting Try it out.

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
The backend connects to a PostgreSQL database through the DATABASE_URL variable. Schema changes are made with migration scripts, never by editing tables by hand.

Before running a migration in production, test it locally first. Take a backup of the production database before any change that removes or renames columns.

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text:
Every change follows the same path:

  1. Create a branch and make the change.
  2. Open a pull request.
  3. A teammate reviews it and the team checks that the build passes.
  4. Merge into main.
  5. Vercel and Heroku detect the merge and deploy the new version automatically.
feature branch --> pull request --> review --> main --> Vercel (frontend) + Heroku (backend)

docs.title: Monitoring and logs
docs.text: What Where Why Frontend build and runtime logs Vercel dashboard Find failed builds and page errors Backend logs Heroku dashboard, Logs Find errors and slow requests Health check /health endpoint Confirm the API is up API testing /docs page Try endpoints without extra tools

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
If a release causes problems:

  1. Open the dashboard for the affected service (Vercel or Heroku).
  2. Redeploy the last working version, or revert the merge commit on main.
  3. Confirm the fix with the health check and by opening the app.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Likely cause Fix Build fails on Vercel Missing NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL or a code error Read the build log and check the variable App shows old content after a release Service worker is serving the cached version Close all app tabs and reopen, or clear site data Frontend cannot reach the API Wrong API address or CORS setting Check NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL and the backend allowed origins Backend crashes on startup Missing config var Check that DATABASE_URL, REDU_AUTH_SECRET and GEMINI_API_KEY are set on Heroku Offline lessons do not sync Learner not signed in or API unreachable Sign in again and check the backend logs AI tutor does not respond Invalid GEMINI_API_KEY or no internet connection Check the key on Heroku and confirm the device is online

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Redu is a Progressive Web App for refugee learners in Uganda. MVP 1 covers Mathematics, English, Biology, Physics and Chemistry, and has five features that match the modules in the System Architecture Diagram

Feature Used by Purpose Learn Learner Study curriculum lessons, with an AI tutor on hand Assessments Learner Find learning gaps and get a catch-up plan View progress Learner See how far you have come and what to do next Offline packages Learner Download lessons and study without internet System management Administrator Monitor usage, learners and curriculum coverage

docs.title: Learn
docs.text:
• Subject and topic navigation: Learners choose a subject and browse S1 and S2 topics in a simple, guided layout.
  • Curriculum-grounded lessons: Lessons are built from approved curriculum files, with linked textbook images, so content stays on syllabus.
  • Flexible explanations: Each concept can be shown as a simple explanation, step by step, a worked example, a visual or practice questions.
  • AI tutor: Learners ask topic questions and get answers in simple English from approved content and reviewed glossary terms.
  • Recommended for you: The home screen suggests the next topics based on the learner's results.

View learn screen

docs.title: Assessments
docs.text:
• Diagnostic check: A short assessment finds what a learner knows, struggles with and may have missed.
  • Practice quizzes: Questions appear one at a time, with a progress bar so learners know how far along they are.
  • Instant evaluation: Answers are evaluated straight away, with feedback and the correct answers.
  • Catch-up plan: Feedback comes with a plan that points to the topics that need work.
  • Fair results: Diagnostic results are tested across learner groups so no group is unfairly disadvantaged.

View assessments screen

docs.title: View Progress
docs.text:
• Progress summary: Completed lessons, quiz results and topics mastered in one place.
  • Topics needing practice: Weaker areas are highlighted so learners know where to focus.
  • Next steps: Every summary ends with a recommended next activity.
  • Recent activity: Learners can look back over what they studied recently.
  • Improvement over time: Baseline and follow-up assessments show how much a learner has improved.

View progress screen

docs.title: Offline Packages
docs.text:
• Download by subject, class, topic and term: Learners choose exactly what they need.
  • Study without internet: Downloaded lessons are saved on the device and open without a connection.
  • Automatic sync: Progress made offline is saved locally and sent to the server when the connection returns.
  • Works on shared devices: The app runs on phones, tablets and school computers, and clears local data when a learner logs out.
  • Trusted packages: Packages are signed, versioned and checked for tampering before use.

View offline screen

docs.title: System Management (Admin PWA)
docs.text:
• System overview: Active learners, usage trends and system health at a glance.
  • Usage and engagement analytics: System-wide data shows how learners use Redu.
  • Learner management: A table of learners with their device and status.
  • Curriculum coverage: Coverage by subject shows where content is complete.
  • Privacy-safe reporting: Reports on small groups are suppressed so no learner can be identified.

View admin dashboard

The Redu PWA is the app Senior 1 and Senior 2 learners use on phones, tablets and shared school computers. It keeps working offline and syncs progress when the connection returns.

docs.title: Where it works
docs.text: Redu is responsive, so the same experience works on smartphones, tablets and school computers, including shared devices.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The Redu Quality Assurance (QA) process ensures that the informational website and student Progressive Web App (PWA) are reliable, accessible, understandable and visually consistent across the devices and connectivity conditions expected by learners.

QA checks more than whether the application loads. It confirms that learners can find the correct subject and topic, understand lessons, complete practice activities, continue learning offline, save their progress and return later without losing their work.

The QA process also protects learner privacy by checking that one learner cannot access another learner’s account, progress, saved content or personal information.

docs.title: QA scope
docs.text:
The frontend QA process covers:

  • Visual consistency with the approved Redu designs.
  • Responsive layouts on smartphones, tablets and desktop computers.
  • Navigation and user interactions.
  • Accessibility and readable content.
  • Browser compatibility.
  • PWA installation and updates.
  • Service-worker behaviour.
  • Offline lessons and approved resources.
  • IndexedDB storage.
  • Progress synchronisation after reconnection.
  • Authentication and learner data separation.
  • Loading, empty, success and error states.
  • Performance on low-cost devices and slow networks.
  • Contact-form behaviour on the informational website.
  • Regression testing after frontend changes.

docs.title: QA approach
docs.text:
Testing should take place throughout development rather than only before release.

The process follows this sequence:

Review the requirement
        ↓
Define the expected user outcome
        ↓
Implement the interface
        ↓
Test the normal user flow
        ↓
Test invalid and interrupted conditions
        ↓
Record and prioritise defects
        ↓
Fix confirmed issues
        ↓
Run regression testing
        ↓
Complete QA sign-off

Each feature should be tested from the learner’s perspective. The team should verify not only whether the technical action succeeds, but also whether the user understands what happened.

docs.title: Test environments
docs.text:
Testing should include the main environments used by Redu learners and project stakeholders.

Environment Purpose Chrome on Android Main mobile browser and PWA installation Chrome on desktop Development and school-computer testing Firefox Browser compatibility Safari on iOS iPhone and iPad behaviour Edge Desktop compatibility Small Android smartphone Small-screen and limited-resource testing Tablet Shared-device and classroom testing Laptop or desktop Wider-screen experience

The team should record the browser version, operating system, device and build or commit being tested.

Recommended viewport sizes are:

360 × 800 — small smartphone
390 × 844 — modern smartphone
768 × 1024 — tablet
1280 × 800 — laptop
1440 × 900 — desktop

docs.title: Functional testing
docs.text:
Functional testing confirms that every important control performs the correct action and gives the user useful feedback.

The team should test:

  • Website navigation links.
  • Mobile menu behaviour.
  • Subject selection.
  • S1 and S2 class selection.
  • Topic selection.
  • Lesson opening and navigation.
  • Glossary and simpler-English explanations.
  • Practice and assessment submission.
  • Progress updates.
  • Recommendations.
  • Offline package downloads.
  • AI tutor interactions.
  • Contact-form submission.
  • Logout and account switching.

Each flow should be tested under normal, invalid, empty, loading and interrupted conditions.

docs.title: Contact-form testing
docs.text:
The QA team should confirm that:

  • Required fields cannot be left empty.
  • Invalid email addresses are rejected.
  • A loading state appears during submission.
  • The submit button prevents accidental duplicate submissions.
  • A success message appears after a successful submission.
  • A useful error message appears when submission fails.
  • Entered information is not unnecessarily lost after a recoverable error.
  • The form does not request sensitive information that is not needed.

Suggested messages include:

Thank you for contacting the Redu team. We have received your message.

We could not send your message. Please check your connection and try again.

docs.title: Student user-flow testing
docs.text:
The core learner journey should be tested from beginning to end.

1. Open Redu.
2. Sign in or complete onboarding.
3. Select S1 or S2.
4. Select a subject.
5. Select a topic.
6. Open a lesson.
7. Read the lesson content.
8. Open a glossary explanation if needed.
9. Ask the AI tutor for support if available.
10. Complete a practice activity.
11. Save or update progress.
12. Close and reopen the application.
13. Confirm that progress is retained.
14. Download content for offline use.
15. Disconnect from the internet.
16. Continue learning offline.
17. Reconnect to the internet.
18. Synchronise progress.
19. Confirm that the update is saved once.

The flow should be tested with both a new learner and a returning learner.

docs.title: Responsive testing
docs.text:
The Redu interface must remain usable on shared smartphones, tablets and desktop computers.

QA should confirm that:

  • Content does not overflow horizontally.
  • Text remains readable without unnecessary zooming.
  • Buttons and controls are large enough for touch interaction.
  • Menus fit within the viewport.
  • Forms are usable on small screens.
  • Cards stack correctly on mobile devices.
  • Images do not hide important content.
  • Lesson navigation remains available in portrait orientation.
  • Landscape orientation does not break the learning experience.
  • Long headings wrap naturally.
  • Dialogues and pop-ups remain fully visible.
  • No important action is pushed outside the screen.

The interface must not assume that the learner has a large screen, a mouse, a keyboard or a fast connection.

docs.title: Accessibility testing
docs.text:
Redu should follow WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility principles where applicable.

QA should check:

  • Keyboard-only navigation.
  • Visible focus indicators.
  • Correct heading order.
  • Semantic HTML.
  • Labels for all form fields.
  • Descriptive names for buttons and links.
  • Alternative text for meaningful images.
  • Empty alternative text for decorative images.
  • Sufficient colour contrast.
  • Accessible error messages.
  • No keyboard traps.
  • Text resizing without loss of content.
  • Reduced-motion support.
  • Clear language and readable line length.
  • Status information that is not communicated through colour alone.

For example, a completed lesson should include a completion label or icon in addition to a green colour. An offline state should display a text label such as Offline or Saved on this device.

docs.title: PWA testing
docs.text:
The PWA should be tested in both the browser and installed application modes.

QA should confirm that:

  • The web app manifest is available.
  • The application has the correct name and short name.
  • Required icons are available.
  • The application can be installed from a supported browser.
  • The installed application opens correctly.
  • The app shell loads when the network is unavailable.
  • Approved resources are available offline.
  • Service-worker registration succeeds.
  • Service-worker updates are handled safely.
  • Old assets are not used after a successful update.
  • Learner data is not unexpectedly deleted during an update.
  • Offline and online states are clearly communicated.
  • The application recovers after a failed update.

Next.js bundles the application during the build process. The service worker is responsible for caching the app shell, approved static resources and offline content. It does not replace Next.js or duplicate the framework’s bundling process.

docs.title: Cache storage and IndexedDB testing
docs.text:
The PWA uses different browser storage mechanisms for different types of data.

Cache Storage:
App shell, static assets and approved cacheable resources.

IndexedDB:
Lessons, offline-package metadata, progress records, assessment drafts and sync events.

QA should verify that:

  • Downloaded lessons are saved correctly.
  • Package versions are recorded.
  • Lesson progress is saved locally.
  • Assessment drafts remain available after a page refresh.
  • Sync events receive unique client identifiers.
  • Replayed events are not stored twice.
  • Offline content is connected to the correct subject and class.
  • Local data is associated with the correct learner.
  • Local data is cleared or isolated correctly after logout.
  • Storage errors produce a clear message.
  • Corrupted or incomplete content is not treated as usable.

docs.title: Offline package testing
docs.text:
Offline packages must be tested before being made available to learners.

QA should verify that:

  • Only published packages can be downloaded.
  • The package title, subject and class are correct.
  • The package version is displayed.
  • The package size is displayed where appropriate.
  • Download progress is visible.
  • Interrupted downloads can be retried.
  • The package checksum is verified.
  • Corrupted packages are rejected.
  • Required lessons are available after download.
  • Supporting images and diagrams open offline.
  • Package content matches the selected subject and class.
  • Withdrawn or outdated packages are handled safely.
  • The learner can remove an offline package when appropriate.

docs.title: Progress synchronisation testing
docs.text:
Offline progress must be saved locally and synchronised safely when the connection returns.

The main test flow is:

1. Log in while online.
2. Open a lesson.
3. Disconnect the device.
4. Change the lesson progress.
5. Confirm that the progress is stored locally.
6. Close and reopen the PWA while offline.
7. Confirm that the progress is still available.
8. Reconnect to the internet.
9. Start synchronisation.
10. Confirm that the server accepts the update once.
11. Repeat the sync request.
12. Confirm that no duplicate progress is created.

QA should also test:

  • Network failure during synchronisation.
  • App closure during synchronisation.
  • Expired login sessions.
  • Duplicate sync events.
  • Partial synchronisation.
  • Invalid content IDs.
  • Server errors.
  • Outdated package versions.
  • Incorrect device time.
  • Multiple offline changes to the same lesson.
  • Synchronisation after a long period offline.

The client device timestamp should not be treated as the authoritative ordering mechanism. The server should record when the event was received and processed.

docs.title: Assessment testing
docs.text:
Assessment testing should confirm that learner answers and progress are not lost.

QA should test:

  • Starting a diagnostic, practice activity or quiz.
  • Displaying the correct question set.
  • Saving an unfinished attempt.
  • Leaving and resuming an attempt.
  • Selecting and changing answers before submission.
  • Submitting an answer once.
  • Handling a slow or interrupted submission.
  • Displaying feedback.
  • Completing an assessment.
  • Saving identified learning gaps.
  • Displaying recommendations.
  • Preventing duplicate attempts caused by repeated clicks.
  • Preserving an offline attempt until it can be synchronised.

docs.title: AI tutor testing
docs.text:
The AI tutor should be tested as a learning-support feature rather than as an unrestricted chatbot.

QA should confirm that:

  • The learner can ask a question from the correct lesson or topic.
  • The request includes the relevant learning context.
  • The response is displayed clearly.
  • The learner can request a simpler explanation.
  • Loading states are shown while the response is being generated.
  • Errors are explained in plain language.
  • Out-of-scope questions are handled safely.
  • Responses are associated with the correct learner and topic.
  • Saved responses can be accessed offline where supported.
  • Personal information is not unnecessarily included in the AI request.
  • The interface does not claim that the AI response is always correct.

docs.title: Authentication and privacy testing
docs.text:
The frontend must protect learner information.

QA should confirm that:

  • Unauthenticated users cannot access protected learner routes.
  • A learner cannot view another learner’s progress.
  • Changing an identifier in a URL or request does not expose another account.
  • Logout removes the active session.
  • Cached private data is not visible after logout.
  • A second learner using the same device sees only their own data.
  • Admin-only screens are not available to student accounts.
  • Session expiry is handled safely.
  • Passwords are never displayed in error messages.
  • Learner codes and personal information are not exposed in logs.
  • AI requests do not include unnecessary personal information.
  • Protected data is not included in public website pages.

docs.title: Performance testing
docs.text:
Performance testing is important because Redu targets learners who may use low-cost devices and slow or unreliable networks.

QA should review:

  • Initial page-load time.
  • Lesson-loading time.
  • Image sizes.
  • JavaScript bundle size.
  • Time required to open downloaded lessons.
  • IndexedDB read and write performance.
  • Offline-package download behaviour.
  • Memory usage during long study sessions.
  • AI response loading behaviour.
  • Performance when many topics are displayed.
  • Recovery after a slow or interrupted connection.

The application should load content progressively. It should not load every subject, topic and lesson at the same time when the learner has selected only one subject.

docs.title: Critical
docs.text:
The product cannot be used or a serious privacy or security problem exists.

Examples:

  • A learner can access another learner’s data.
  • The application cannot open after installation.
  • Progress is permanently deleted.
  • Authentication exposes sensitive information.
  • Offline data is corrupted.

docs.title: High
docs.text:
A major learning or product flow is blocked.

Examples:

  • A learner cannot open lessons.
  • Offline progress cannot synchronise.
  • Assessment answers disappear.
  • The PWA cannot be installed.
  • The contact form loses submitted information.

docs.title: Medium
docs.text:
The feature works incorrectly but a workaround exists.

Examples:

  • A recommendation opens the wrong lesson.
  • A glossary control fails on one browser.
  • An image is missing while the lesson text remains available.
  • A non-critical offline package update is delayed.

docs.title: Low
docs.text:
The issue does not prevent the user from completing the task.

Examples:

  • Minor spacing inconsistency.
  • Small icon misalignment.
  • Slight colour difference.
  • Non-critical text-wrapping issue.

docs.title: Defect report format
docs.text:
Each defect should include:

Title:
Environment:
Device and browser:
Build or commit:
Precondition:
Steps to reproduce:
Expected result:
Actual result:
Severity:
Screenshot or recording:
Related requirement:

docs.title: Example defect report
docs.text:
Title: Lesson progress is duplicated after reconnection

Environment: Chrome on Android
Device: Shared Android smartphone
Build: feature/offline-progress
Precondition: Biology S1 package is downloaded

Steps:
1. Open the Cell Structure lesson.
2. Disconnect the network.
3. Complete the lesson.
4. Close and reopen the PWA.
5. Reconnect to the network.
6. Start synchronisation.
7. Repeat synchronisation.

Expected result:
The lesson remains completed and the progress event is processed once.

Actual result:
Two identical progress events are created.

Severity:
High

docs.title: Regression testing
docs.text:
Regression testing should be completed after changes to:

  • Navigation.
  • Authentication.
  • Service-worker logic.
  • IndexedDB schemas.
  • Offline packages.
  • Progress handling.
  • Assessment submission.
  • AI tutor screens.
  • Shared design components.
  • Responsive layouts.
  • Brand colours or typography.
  • Contact-form behaviour.

A change to a shared component should be checked in both:

Informational website
Student PWA

The team should not assume that a component that works on the homepage will automatically work correctly inside the learning experience.

docs.title: Definition of Done
docs.text:
A frontend task is complete when:

  • The approved design has been implemented.
  • The feature works on mobile, tablet and desktop layouts.
  • Loading, empty, success and error states are included.
  • Keyboard navigation works.
  • Controls have accessible labels.
  • Offline behaviour has been tested where applicable.
  • Learner data is correctly isolated.
  • No new console errors or warnings are introduced.
  • Relevant tests have been recorded.
  • Another team member has reviewed the change.
  • Documentation has been updated where the behaviour changed.
  • No critical or high-severity defects remain open.
  • Final regression testing is complete.

docs.title: QA sign-off checklist
docs.text:
[ ] Website navigation works
[ ] PWA navigation works
[ ] Responsive layouts have been checked
[ ] Redu colours and typography are consistent
[ ] Logo usage is correct
[ ] Contact-form validation works
[ ] Subject and class selection works
[ ] Topics and lessons open correctly
[ ] Glossary and simpler explanations work
[ ] Practice and assessment flows work
[ ] AI tutor loading and error states work
[ ] Progress is saved correctly
[ ] Offline packages download correctly
[ ] Downloaded lessons and images work offline
[ ] IndexedDB data persists correctly
[ ] Service-worker behaviour has been checked
[ ] Synchronisation does not create duplicates
[ ] Logout protects the previous learner’s data
[ ] Accessibility checks are complete
[ ] Performance has been reviewed on a low-cost device
[ ] No critical or high-severity defects remain
[ ] Final regression testing is complete
[ ] QA results have been reviewed by the team

docs.title: QA summary
docs.text:
The Redu QA process ensures that the product is visually consistent, technically reliable and suitable for real learning conditions.

The main quality goal is for a learner to:

Open Redu
    ↓
Find the correct subject and topic
    ↓
Understand the lesson
    ↓
Continue learning offline
    ↓
Save progress safely
    ↓
Reconnect without losing work
    ↓
Access only their own information

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Redu is designed for shared devices, intermittent connectivity and limited data access, so security and privacy controls focus on three areas: protecting learner data on the device, protecting data sent to the AI provider, and controlling who can access what.

Security and Privacy Requirements Document.

docs.title: Security architecture
docs.text: System Security Architecture Diagram

docs.title: Key controls
docs.text: Area Control Sessions Inactivity logout after 10 minutes, with a warning first; absolute maximum session of 8 hours Sign-in Lock-out after 5 failed sign-ins in 15 minutes (QA plan value) Administrators Multi-factor authentication (MFA) required Data collected Name, email address and class level only Encryption Encrypted at rest; TLS 1.2 or higher in transit AI requests Credentials stay server-side; pseudonymous learner IDs; names and emails redacted AI usage Quota of 100 questions per day (QA plan value) Offline packages Signed, versioned and hash-verified Retention Automated deletion after 3 months (period still to be formally confirmed)

docs.title: Security requirements

AI requests only through the Redu API; answers grounded in approved curriculum; NOT_IN_CURRICULUM fallback; server-side validation of sync events; idempotent sync; rate limiting and AI quotas; prompt-injection and AI safety testing Must have SR-004 Authorization Role-based access control; docs.title: Privacy requirements
docs.text: Area Requirement Personal data Collect only what is needed for accounts, learning, diagnostics, progress and system operation Purpose Use learner data only for learning services, diagnostics, progress support, security and required administration Data minimisation Collect name, email address and class level Storage Approved Redu storage locations only, with access controls and encryption Access Learners see their own data; staff access is role-based and limited to operational need Sharing Tutor requests go to the approved AI provider only after minimisation and redaction Retention and deletion Periods must be formally decided before build or pilot; automated deletion after 3 months User rights A process for access, correction and deletion requests Cross-border transfer AI processing may happen outside Uganda; provider terms, location and safeguards must be reviewed and approved before deployment

docs.text: Service Purpose Data shared Requirement Google Gemini API and File Search AI study support and curriculum retrieval Pseudonymous learner prompts and approved curriculum content Server-side API key; provider terms and processing location reviewed; no unnecessary identifiers; monitor quotas and cost

docs.title: Security testing
docs.text:
All of the following must be completed before the learner pilot.

Test What it covers Source code review Peer review plus static analysis (SAST) Dependency and security scanning SCA, secret scanning and infrastructure-as-code checks in CI/CD Penetration testing API, PWA, authorization and upload workflow, plus a dynamic (DAST) scan of a staging build Privacy review DPIA, consent model, redaction, retention and deletion Prompt-injection and AI safety testing Jailbreaks, injection through uploaded files, off-syllabus requests, the fallback and output filtering Diagnostic fairness testing Results compared across learner groups, exceptions documented Safeguarding testing A harm disclosure reaches the named human contact Offline integrity testing Signature and hash checks, tampered packages, forged and replayed sync events, offline session expiry Authorization testing Automated proof that a learner cannot read another learner's records or reach staff functions Load and abuse testing Rate limits, AI quotas, upload limits and the AI-outage fallback

docs.title: Compliance
docs.text:
• Uganda's Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2019 (lawful basis and consent, minimisation, safeguards, cross-border transfer, breach notification, individual rights). Any registration obligation is to be confirmed by legal counsel.
  • OWASP Top 10 as the reference list of web application risks.
  • This project's security and privacy requirements.
  • UNHCR data protection principles (purpose limitation, confidentiality, minimisation) and partner child safeguarding policies, including a protocol for disclosures of harm.
  • GDPR and ISO/IEC 27001 as benchmarks where EU funders or partners are involved.
  • AI provider data-processing terms approved before deployment, covering no-training terms, retention and processing location.
